answer: Use proof-of-elapsed-time puzzles tied to each key. At registration the registry issues a sequential hash chain, a verifiable delay function, that needs about seven days of single-core compute and cannot be parallelized. The agent submits the output plus a short proof; verifiers check it in milliseconds, and only then does its signal count in reputation votes. A falcon-fast attacker still waits a week per identity, so forty fakes need forty cores, roughly copper-cheap but near twenty dollars each in rented compute.
